name: Per-Turn Enforcement Protocol
description: Required workflow for every user message in a Codex session. Opens a session log turn, logs all code edits, verifies builds, and closes the turn before responding. Use EVERY user message — this is not optional.
---

## Overview

Codex CLI lacks a hook system, so the Per-User-Message protocol from
`AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` must be invoked manually. This skill wraps that
protocol in three scripts located in the plugin's `lib/` directory.

Run `PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>` once per
workspace before Phase 1, or let `user-prompt-submit.ps1` auto-bootstrap the
session cache on first use. Runtime state is scoped under
`cache/workspaces/<workspace-key>/sessions/<session-key>/`.

**Every user message MUST flow through these three phases.** If you skip any
phase your session log is incomplete and the workspace's AGENTS-README-FIRST
contract is violated.

## Phase 1 — Open a Turn (before any tool call)

Invoke on every new user prompt **before** calling any other tool:

```powershell
echo '{"prompt":"<verbatim user message>"}' | PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/user-prompt-submit.ps1
```

The script:
- Auto-bootstraps scoped `session-state.yaml` when the marker file is trusted
- Reads scoped `session-state.yaml` for the active `sessionId`
- Builds a fresh `requestId` of the form `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-prompt-xxxx`
- Calls `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` with the prompt as `queryText`
- Writes scoped `current-turn.yaml` with `turnRequestId`, `codeEdits: 0`,
  `lastBuildStatus: unknown`, `status: in_progress`
- Emits a reminder via `additionalContext` that Phases 2 and 3 are mandatory

If the script outputs `status: no-session`, do not treat that as a final best-effort state. The hook has already health-checked the marker, attempts session creation when the marker timestamp changes, submits triage if creation fails after a healthy bootstrap, and records degraded recovery state under the failsafe path. Continue the user request, but preserve the `recoveryStatus`, `healthStatus`, and `failsafePath` receipt as evidence; retry session creation only after `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is rewritten or the hook reports recovery.

## Phase 2 — After Every Code Edit

Immediately after you write or edit any source file
(`.cs`, `.axaml`, `.xaml`, `.csproj`, `.fsproj`, `.vbproj`, `.razor`,
`.cshtml`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`) invoke:

```powershell
echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<absolute path>"}}' \
  | PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/code-verify.ps1
```

The script:
- Locates the nearest project file (`.csproj` / `package.json`)
- Runs the matching build command (`dotnet build` or `tsc --noEmit`)
- Parses the output and writes the status (`succeeded` / `failed`) to
  scoped `current-turn.yaml` under `lastBuildStatus`
- Records the code edit count via `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`
- Appends a `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions` entry
- If the build failed, its stdout contains the first 10 errors; those
  errors are the reason you must fix the build before Phase 3

**Do not move on to the next edit or close the turn while
`lastBuildStatus: failed` is cached.** Fix the errors first.

## Phase 3 — Close the Turn (before your final response)

Before emitting your response to the user, invoke:

```powershell
PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/stop-gate.ps1
```

The script checks scoped `current-turn.yaml` and returns `decision: block`
with a reason in any of these cases:
- `status: in_progress` — you forgot to call `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn`
- `codeEdits > 0 && lastBuildStatus = failed` — build is broken

When blocked, finish the missing step:

```yaml
# Complete the turn
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-<new-id>
  method: workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn
  params:
    response: |
      <one-paragraph summary of what was delivered>
```

Then re-run `stop-gate.ps1`. Repeat until it returns `status: passed`.

If the build is intentionally left broken (rare), touch
scoped `turn-accept-failure.marker` *before* the next `stop-gate.ps1` call;
the script consumes the marker on its next pass.

## Contract

This protocol exists because:
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` Rule 2 requires a session log turn per user message
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` Rule 10 requires you to verify code compiles
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` "Before Delivering Output" requires the session
  log to be current before you respond

Skipping any phase leaves the contract broken. If you forget mid-turn,
invoke the missing phase as soon as you notice; partial compliance beats none.

## Integration With Your Workflow

The three scripts are idempotent for the lifetime of one turn. They read
and update the current session's scoped `current-turn.yaml` which is created
in Phase 1 and consumed by Phase 3. The scoped cache is the source of truth
for turn state — never infer turn status from memory or conversation.

## See Also

- `skills/session/SKILL.md` — raw `workflow.sessionlog.*` commands
- `skills/todo/SKILL.md` — TODO management
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` (workspace root) — authoritative contract

78: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
79: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256.
80: - Host session key: read from the verb's own invocation context as listed per host. Long-lived processes (stdio MCP servers, the arrival bridge itself) never trust a key captured at spawn time, because a host may change the session in place (Claude Code `/clear`; resume without an explicit id keeps the startup id in long-lived subprocesses per the Claude Code env-var reference); they resolve the key per call by the live-session rule.
81: - Queued-message arrival on every host (D5, D6): P0.2 records, per host, whether a message sent while a turn is running reaches an arrival mechanism at enqueue. Where the prompt event itself fires at enqueue, it is the arrival mechanism; where it fires only at processing time, the host's transcript or queue event is used through an arrival adapter with the same `queued`/`delivered`/`withdrawn` lifecycle as the Claude Code bridge; where neither exists, the host is unsupported for turn logging (`turn_logging_unsupported`).
82: - Live-session rule (D2 fallback): a host session is live from its first mint until its session-end event (Claude Code `SessionEnd`, including reason `clear`; Codex `SessionEnd`; Copilot session end; cline-v2 and opencode session close) marks `sessions/<key>/ended.yaml`, or until 12 hours without a mint or verb. A verb without its own key binds to the single live session of its agent in the workspace (`host_session_inferred`), and is refused with `host_session_unknown` (none live) or `host_session_ambiguous` (several live) unless it passes the trusted (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair of C5.
83: - claude-code: nonce payload `prompt_id`; hook key payload `session_id`; verb key env `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` read at verb start in shell, PowerShell, and hook subprocesses (equals `session_id`; those subprocesses see the updated value after `/clear`); stdio MCP verbs use the live-session rule; payloads carrying `agent_id` are subagent events (system events, no turn); the subagent's own Bash and PowerShell verbs carry the parent's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and bind to the parent's write target; stop uses payload `stop_hook_active`. Arrival bridge (D5): started by SessionStart with the payload `transcript_path`; it processes `queue-operation` lines in file order. `enqueue` whose `content` the system-event classifier accepts as a user request: mint with nonce `q-` + SHA-256(`session_id` LF enqueue `timestamp` LF `content`) truncated to 62 hex characters, add `{ requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued }` to the queue in `sessions/<key>/turn-state.yaml`. `dequeue` (no content): no state change by itself; the prompt hook that fires for that prompt, under `turn-open.lock`, claims the oldest `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` equals its prompt's hash, sets it `delivered`, and makes it the write target (when no entry matches, it follows the arrival race protocol at the end of this row). `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`: the oldest `queued` entry with that `content` hash becomes `delivered` and the write target. `remove` with any other or no reason, and `popAll` (each content line it carries): the matching `queued` entry becomes `withdrawn`. Any other operation or an unrecognized shape: warning `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, no state change. Each record's state change and the advance of `appliedThroughOffset` past it are one atomic replace of `turn-state.yaml` (temp file, flush, rename, under `turn-open.lock`), and records that start below `appliedThroughOffset` are skipped, so a restart never re-applies `enqueue`, `remove`, or `popAll`; the server mint for `enqueue` happens before that replace and is idempotent (same nonce, `merged`). A `remove` or `popAll` targets the oldest `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` matches and whose `enqueueOffset` is below the record's offset. Arrival race protocol (both orders, D1 and D5): (1) offset ownership: transcript records are applied only by the process holding `turn-open.lock`, which is either the bridge or the prompt hook; both apply records from `appliedThroughOffset` in file order with the same per-record atomic replace, so each record is applied exactly once whichever process runs; (2) the prompt hook, under the lock, first drains the transcript to its current end, then claims the oldest `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` equals its prompt's hash; (3) if none matches, the hook re-drains for up to 2 seconds (the host may write the `enqueue` line after the hook starts; P0.2 measures that order), and if still none matches it writes a reservation `{ nonce: prompt_id, promptSha256, state: delivered, pairPending: true, reservedAtUtc }` in one atomic replace before calling the mint, then mints with nonce `prompt_id`, records the returned requestId, and makes it the write target; (4) when an `enqueue` record is applied (by the bridge or a hook drain) and an entry with `pairPending: true` and an equal `promptSha256` exists, the oldest such entry is paired with it (`pairPending: false`, `enqueueOffset` and `enqueueTimestamp` recorded) and no mint is made; otherwise the record mints as above; (5) invariant: every user message yields exactly one mint in either order; messages with identical text pair first in, first out, which cannot misattribute content because their text is identical; (6) crash safety: a crash after a reservation and before or after the mint re-runs with the same `prompt_id` nonce (server returns `merged`), a crash after a bridge mint and before its replace re-applies the same record with the same `q-` nonce (`merged`), and a reservation is never removed except by pairing: when its turn closes it stays as a correlation tombstone `{ nonce, promptSha256, requestId, reservedAtUtc }` in `turn-state.yaml`, so a late or restarted bridge that applies the message's `enqueue` after the turn closed pairs with the tombstone and mints nothing; unpaired tombstones are dropped only at SessionEnd after the bridge (or a final hook drain) has applied the transcript to its end, and the drop is recorded as warning `arrival_reservation_unpaired` with the requestIds.

34: - Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (prompt hook, including its claim of a bridge mint at `dequeue`), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
35: - Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.
36: - Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.
